title: Dissecting racial bias in an algorithm used to manage the health of populations
supports_claim: The study found that a widely used health-management algorithm predicting cost rather than illness produced racial bias; changing the target would increase Black patients receiving additional help from 17.7% to 46.5%.
limitations: The study concerns a particular commercial algorithm and care-management context, not a conversational symptom-triage assistant or all populations.

title: External Validation of a Widely Implemented Proprietary Sepsis Prediction Model in Hospitalized Patients
publisher: JAMA Internal Medicine / National Library of Medicine
supports_claim: An external validation study found that, at the selected Epic Sepsis Model threshold, 183 of 2,552 sepsis hospitalizations had a model score of 6 or higher before or within three hours after sepsis and did not receive timely antibiotics.
limitations: The study evaluates one proprietary inpatient model at one academic medical center; it does not establish causation for treatment outcomes or performance of CareBridge.

title: Chatbot that offered bad advice for eating disorders taken down
supports_claim: NPR reported user screenshots of dieting and weight-management guidance from NEDA's Tessa chatbot and reported that NEDA suspended the chatbot after content received by some testers may have been harmful and unrelated to the programme.
limitations: The article reports an incident and accounts from NEDA, users, and the vendor; it does not independently establish the technical mechanism, prevalence, clinical causality, or performance of all health chatbots.

title: Regulation of predictive analytics in medicine: Algorithms must meet regulatory standards of clinical benefit
supports_claim: This peer-reviewed perspective argues that predictive algorithms in medicine need evidence of clinical benefit and discusses limits of regulatory evaluation.
limitations: It is a perspective article, not a product-specific regulatory decision or validation study.

title: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689: Artificial Intelligence Act
publisher: Official Journal of the European Union
supports_claim: Article 6 provides high-risk classification rules for an AI system that is a product or safety component covered by listed Union harmonisation legislation when the stated conditions are met.
limitations: Applicability depends on intended purpose, medical-device or product-law scope, market placement, conformity-assessment facts, and dates; it is not a legal opinion for CareBridge.

title: Law No. 91/2025/QH15 on Personal Data Protection
publisher: National Assembly of Vietnam / Government Portal
supports_claim: Vietnam's Personal Data Protection Law took effect on 2026-01-01, requiring an up-to-date legal and privacy assessment before CareBridge processes real-user symptom text or referral metadata.
limitations: The publication metadata does not determine CareBridge's controller or processor roles, consent basis, health-data duties, retention, security, or transfer obligations.

title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0)
publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
supports_claim: NIST AI RMF describes governance, mapping, measurement, and management activities for trustworthy AI risk management.
limitations: The voluntary framework is not a certification and does not prove that a control is effective.

title: WHO calls for safe and ethical AI for health
supports_claim: WHO warns that health-related large-language-model outputs can appear authoritative yet be incorrect or contain serious errors and calls for clear evidence of benefit before widespread routine-health use.
limitations: Global guidance does not set CareBridge-specific clinical thresholds or determine Vietnam legal status.

title: Decree No. 356/2025/ND-CP detailing implementation of the Personal Data Protection Law
supports_claim: Decree 356/2025/ND-CP details implementation of Vietnam's Personal Data Protection Law and took effect on 2026-01-01.
limitations: Counsel must apply the decree to the final CareBridge data flow, roles, consent, retention, security, and transfer facts.

title: Law No. 134/2025/QH15 on Artificial Intelligence
publisher: National Assembly of Vietnam / Government Portal
supports_claim: Vietnam's Artificial Intelligence Law took effect on 2026-03-01 and is relevant to an assessment of a future public symptom-routing service.
limitations: The official publication title and effective date do not by themselves classify CareBridge; counsel must apply the final intended purpose and operating facts.

title: Decision No. 33/2026/QD-TTg issuing the list of high-risk AI systems
publisher: Prime Minister of Vietnam / Government Portal
supports_claim: Decision 33/2026/QD-TTg issues Vietnam's list of high-risk AI systems and took effect on 2026-08-15.
limitations: The title and effective date do not establish that CareBridge is listed; a legal review must map the final intended purpose and service boundary to the instrument.

title: Ethics and governance of artificial intelligence for health
supports_claim: WHO guidance states that humans should remain in control of health-care systems and medical decisions and that AI for health should be evaluated for safety, equity, accountability, and responsiveness.
limitations: The guidance is global and principled; it does not replace local legal or product-specific clinical validation.

title: Collision Between Vehicle Controlled by Developmental Automated Driving System and Pedestrian, Tempe, Arizona
supports_claim: The NTSB investigation of the 2018 Tempe crash identified deficiencies involving safety-risk assessment, operator monitoring, oversight, and automation complacency in the developmental automated-driving-system test.
limitations: The report analyzes one United States crash and does not establish performance of another automated-driving system or prove that one human-review design prevents all incidents.

title: Oversight Board overturns Meta's decision in Cambodian Prime Minister case
supports_claim: The Oversight Board found that a political video containing threats against opponents violated Meta's violence policy and required removal, illustrating the need for context-specific and accountable review of high-reach political-content decisions.
limitations: The Board is independent but funded by Meta; the decision concerns one content item and platform policy, not all political moderation or CareBridge.

title: FCC fines man behind election interference scheme $6 million for sending illegal robocalls that used deepfake generative AI technology
supports_claim: The FCC adopted a $6 million fine against Steve Kramer for illegal spoofed robocalls using an AI-generated clone of President Biden's voice to tell potential New Hampshire primary voters not to vote.
limitations: This is a specific U.S. telecommunications enforcement action; it does not estimate changed votes or establish duties for a Vietnamese text-summary prototype.
